The '''Sethi model''' was developed by [[Suresh P. Sethi]] and describes the process of how sales evolve over time in response to [[advertising]].<ref name="sethi83">{{Cite journal |last=Sethi |first=S. P. |year=1983 |title=Deterministic and Stochastic Optimization of a Dynamic Advertising Model |journal=Optimal Control Applications and Methods |volume=4 |issue=2 |pages=179–184 |doi=10.1002/oca.4660040207 |s2cid=123673289 }}</ref><ref name="Sethi00" /> The model assumes that the rate of change in sales depend on three effects: response to advertising that acts positively on the unsold portion of the market, the loss due to forgetting or possibly due to competitive factors that act negatively on the sold portion of the market, and a random effect that can go either way.

[[Suresh P. Sethi|Suresh Sethi]] published his paper "Deterministic and [[Stochastic optimization|Stochastic Optimization]] of a Dynamic Advertising Model" in 1983.<ref name="sethi83" /> The Sethi model is a modification as well as a stochastic extension of  the Vidale-Wolfe advertising model.<ref name=":16">{{Cite journal |last1=Vidale |first1=M. L. |last2=Wolfe |first2=H. B. |year=1957 |title=An Operations-Research Study of Sales Response to Advertising |journal=Operations Research |volume=5 |issue=3 |pages=370–381 |doi=10.1287/opre.5.3.370 }}</ref> The model and its competitive and multi-echelon channel extensions have been used extensively in the literature.<ref name=":5">{{Cite journal|last1=Kennedy|first1=Adrian Patrick|last2=Sethi|first2=Suresh P.|last3=Siu|first3=Chi Chung|last4=Yam|first4=Sheung Chi Phillip|date=2021-07-26|title=Cooperative Advertising in a Dynamic Three-Echelon Supply Chain|journal=Production and Operations Management|volume=30|issue=11|pages=3881–3905|doi=10.1111/poms.13487|s2cid=236272112|issn=1059-1478|via=}}</ref><ref name="Sorger89">{{Cite journal |last=Sorger |first=G. |year=1989 |title=Competitive Dynamic Advertising: A Modification of the Case Game |journal=Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control |volume=13 |issue=1 |pages=55–80 |doi=10.1016/0165-1889(89)90011-0 }}</ref><ref name="CV92">{{Cite journal |last1=Chintagunta |first1=P. ==Model==

The Sethi advertising model or simply the Sethi model provides a sales-advertising dynamics in the form of the following [[stochastic differential equation]]:

: <math> dX_t =\left(rU_t\sqrt{1-X_t} - \delta X_t\right)\,dt+\sigma(X_t)\,dz_t, \qquad X_0=x</math>.

Where:
*  <math>X_t</math> is the market share at  time <math>t</math>
*  <math>U_t</math> is the rate of advertising at time <math>t</math>
*  <math>r</math> is the coefficient of the effectiveness of advertising
*  <math>\delta</math> is the decay constant
*  <math>\sigma(X_t)</math> is the diffusion coefficient
*  <math>z_t</math> is the [[Wiener process]] (Standard [[Brownian motion]]); <math>dz_t</math> is known as [[White noise]].

===Explanation===

The rate of change in sales depend on three effects: response to advertising that acts positively on the unsold portion of the market via <math>r</math>, the loss due to forgetting or possibly due to competitive factors that act negatively on the sold portion of the market via <math>\delta</math>, and a random effect using a diffusion or White noise term that can go either way.

*  The coefficient <math>r</math> is the coefficient of the effectiveness of advertising innovation.
*  The coefficient <math>\delta</math> is the decay constant.
*  The square-root term brings in the so-called word-of-mouth effect at least at low sales levels.<ref name="sethi83" /><ref name="Sorger89" />
*  The diffusion term <math>\sigma(X_t)dz_t</math> brings in the random effect.

===Example of an optimal advertising problem===

Subject to the Sethi model above with the initial market share <math>x</math>, consider the following objective function:

: <math>V(x) = \max_{U_t \geq 0} \;E\left[ \int_0^\infty e^{-\rho t}(\pi X_t-U_t^2)\,dt\right],</math>

where <math>\pi</math> denotes the sales revenue corresponding to the total market, i.e., when <math>x = 1</math>, and <math>\rho > 0</math> denotes the discount rate.

The function <math>V(x)</math> is known as the [[value function]] for this problem, and it is shown to be<ref name="Sethi00">Sethi, S.P. (2021). ''Optimal Control Theory: Applications to Management Science and Economics''. Fourth Edition. Springer.  pp. 354-356. {{isbn|978-3-319-98236-6|978-3-319-98237-3}}. http://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-98237-3</ref>

: <math>
V(x)=\bar\lambda x+ \frac{\bar\lambda^2 r^2}{4
\rho},
</math>

where

: <math>
\bar\lambda=\frac{\sqrt{(\rho+\delta)^2+r^2
\pi}-(\rho+\delta)}{r^2/2}.
</math>

The [[optimal control]] for this problem is<ref name="Sethi00" />

: <math> U^*_t = u^*(X_t)=\frac{r\bar\lambda \sqrt{1-\ X_t}}{2} = \begin{cases}
{} > \bar{u} & \text{if } X_t < \bar{x}, \\
{} = \bar{u} & \text{if } X_t = \bar{x}, \\
{} < \bar{u} & \text{if } X_t > \bar{x},
\end{cases} </math>

where

: <math>
\bar x= \frac{r^2 \bar\lambda /2}{r^2 \bar\lambda /2+\delta}
</math>

and

: <math>
\bar u=\frac{r\bar\lambda \sqrt{1-\bar x}}{2}.
</math>

==Extensions of the Sethi model==

* Competitive model: Nash differential games<ref name="Sorger89" /><ref name="PS04" /><ref name="BKPS05" /><ref name="NPS08" /><ref name="EricEJOR" /><ref name="EricOR" /><ref name=":0">{{Cite book|last1=Rong|first1=Zhang|last2=Qingzhong|first2=Ren|date=May 2013|chapter=Equivalence between Sethi advertising model and a scalar LQ differential game|pages=1244–1247|doi=10.1109/ccdc.2013.6561115|title=2013 25th Chinese Control and Decision Conference (CCDC)|isbn=978-1-4673-5534-6|s2cid=26614539}}</ref><ref name=":4" /><ref name=":6" /><ref name=":7" /><ref name=":8" /><ref name=":9" /><ref name=":10" /><ref name=":13" /><ref name=":14" /><ref name=":15" />
